analysis_notes.summary: Torah #272 is a five-sentence practical ruling (כְּלָל גָּדוֹל) with no bechina language. The Rebbe cites Psalms 95:7 ('הַיּוֹם אִם בְּקוֹלוֹ תִשְׁמָעוּ') and gives a single unified instruction: do not think beyond the current day or hour, whether in livelihood or in avodah. The teaching uses one rhetorical simile — 'כְּאִלּוּ הוּא מַשָּׂא כָּבֵד' (it appears like a heavy burden) — but this is not a bechina equation; it is a psychological description using 'כְּאִלּוּ' (as if). There is no 'הוּא בְּחִינַת', 'נִקְרָא', or equivalent formula anywhere in the text. No concepts are linked by shared nature; the entire Torah is one eitza-type instruction (how to approach avodah) with no bechina sub-structure to map.
